decisions.reason: As a more consumer-oriented offer that sits less squarely in the firm's core industrial-technology aspiration set, it is more likely to underperform expectations and have resources shifted to stronger core ventures.
These modular waste-to-energy extensions build directly on the established business, so boundedly rational management would likely retain them while market feedback is still emerging.
The waste-oil-to-energy plant is strongly aligned with the firm's R&D-intensive capabilities and its prominent presentation suggests commitment, making retention likely despite early uncertainty.
Although somewhat more exploratory than the core offer, the plastic-waste-to-fuel plant still fits the firm's technological trajectory and available slack supports keeping it on the market for now.
